modifications: Unrigged Tripo export in 9 parts (405,368 triangles, three 2048 px textures: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material), standing upright on her two feet with both wings spread, facing +Z. Welded across UV seams and the seams between parts (29 edges split at T-junctions, 5 pinholes filled, no open edge left), decimated as one mesh with the head and the beak keeping 1.6 times the share of the rest (10,080 of 37,499 triangles: her face is seen close up), the wings' trailing edges clean, and split back into its 9 parts, closed (remake/tools/blender-decimate.py, Blender 5.2; kept as source/pteranodon-parts.glb, which the command reproduces byte for byte). Baked by remake/tools/bake/bake-quadruped.js with kind=pterosaur (winged-rig.js and winged-clips.js; run with bake-character.mjs): turned to face +X, scaled to a 7.5 m wingspan (4.12 m to the top of her crest), stood on the ground with the root midway between her soles; the parts told apart by position and seams (two legs on the ground, two wings reaching out across the span, the head with its crest the highest part, the beak holding the nose and touching the head, the body touching both legs, an arm between each wing and the body); her head, which Tripo turned 19 degrees to her right, turned back 18.7 degrees about the top of her neck, the turn fading out 0.5 m down the neck; rigged with 31 bones; welded into one closed, consistently wound skin (23,412 vertices at 18,751 places, one sliver dropped: 37,498 triangles) whose seams share their weights; nine clips authored in code; one skinned mesh with one matte single-sided material (roughness 0.62, no metalness, normal map at 0.5), base colour (no recolour) and normal map as 1024 px JPEG, the metal/roughness map dropped. Then the face pass and the mouth pass (below).
membranes: Tripo made each wing membrane a closed thin shell about 3.5 cm thick (2.8 to 5 cm), not an open sheet, and its seams with the arm, the body and the leg weld exactly. So the membranes stay in the one closed skin and are drawn single-sided like the rest of her: each face shows from its own side, and the two faces of a shell share their weights, so they bend as one. Two-sided thin sheets would mean collapsing each shell to one face and drawing it double-sided (a double-sided character that fills the frame costs about 0.7 ms more on the reference laptop, STYLE.md section 12) or as a second, flipped copy, with a seam to hide where the sheet meets the arm, for nothing gained at her size on screen.
rig: Our bake tool with kind=pterosaur (winged-rig.js). Bones: root, Hips (1.43 m up), Spine, Chest (between the shoulders, 2.02 m up), Neck, Neck2, Neck3, Head (at the top of the neck, 2.85 m up; the head with its crest and the beak ride it rigidly), Tail1-Tail3; the legs as Grameðla's, named as the engine's footing plants a biped: LeftThigh/RightThigh, LeftShin/RightShin, LeftFoot/RightFoot; on each wing LeftUpperArm/RightUpperArm (the shoulder 0.24 m out), Forearm (the elbow 0.99 m out), Wrist (1.68 m), Claws (the three small clawed fingers, rigid) and Finger1, Finger2, Finger3 (the long fourth finger, its joints 2.12, 2.67 and 3.21 m out, the tip at 3.75 m); the Jaw from the mouth pass under the Head; identity rest rotations. The body follows the chain by where it lies along the line through the joints; a leg blends at the knee and the ankle over the planes that halve them, the thigh's top fading into the hips; an arm and the wing's leading edge follow UpperArm to Finger3 by where they lie along the line through their joints; the limbs' shares spread into the body as a harmonic field over 0.53 m, except along the middle of her back, where a strip as wide as her shoulders follows the spine alone. A membrane is held along its seams (the arm's, the body's and the thigh's weights there) and along its leading edge (within 9 cm of the long finger, 4.5 cm of the arm's line); everywhere else its weights are a harmonic field of all the bones that hold its edges at once (eleven a side), so it blends smoothly from the long finger at the tip to the forearm, the body and the thigh at its inner trailing corner. A point on one face of the shell and the point facing it on the other (within 9 cm, the normal turned the other way: 2,305 and 2,369 of the wings' 2,857 and 2,914 places) are eased together and share one set of weights, cut to four bones once for all of them. Clips (winged-clips.js): idle 4.0 s (standing on her feet and the knuckles of her folded wings: a slow breath, the head looking about a little, the folded fingers and the tail swaying; the hips stay still, so the legs keep their rest pose and footing plants the feet); walk 1.6 s, 1.15 m a cycle (0.72 m/s; a foot down 62.5 % of the cycle, landing flat and sweeping back at exactly that speed, the knuckle on the same side a quarter cycle later, so she walks on four points as pterosaurs did); kink 2.4 s (a friendly nod); happy 2.4 s (a hop on the spot with a flutter of half-open wings; the clip keys the legs); takeOff 3.2 s, played once (a crouch, the wings unfolding in stages, a leap and two strong beats up to flying height; its last pose is fly's first); fly 1.4 s (a calm wingbeat, the wings 36 degrees above level at the top and 24 below at the bottom, the body level 2.6 m up and 5 degrees nose-up, the legs trailing, the head steady); glide 6.0 s (the wings held out, banking 9 degrees to one side and the other); land 3.0 s, played once (from fly's first pose down to the ground, a flare and a soft landing at 2.1 s, the wings folding into idle's first pose); carry 3.6 s (flying with a child on her back: two slow, shallow beats, the hips neither bobbing nor pitching, so the back under the seat stays steady and level). takeOff and land carry once in their extras, so the actor plays them once and holds the last pose. In the flying clips the hips are held at flying height: a scene moves her root through the air. The feet stay planted in idle and kink; in a scene the engine's footing plants them in walks, starts, stops and turns on the spot.

seat.note: Where Egill sits in carry, for a saddle (riding.js on the kafli1 branch): the top of her back just behind the shoulders, between the wings, on her middle line, found by the bake in carry's first pose. A saddle follows the Spine bone at `local` (metres, in that bone's frame; rest rotations are identity, so its axes are hers: X forward, Y up, Z her right); `carryPose` and `bindPose` are the same point in her model's frame. Through carry it moves less than 1 cm and tilts less than 1 degree, and the back under it stays within 5 mm of it (the test puts a stand-in object on the bone there). riding.js measures the back in the bind pose, where her back stands upright, so for her the saddle needs this bone and point (or a pose to measure in) rather than its own search.

pose: Rest (bind) pose as Tripo's: standing upright on her two feet, the torso leaning back about 50 degrees from level, both wings spread out to the sides with the membranes hanging below them, the long crest sweeping back; faces +X; 7.5 m across the wings, 4.12 m high, 4.62 m from tail to beak tip.
sourceTextures: three 2048 px JPEG: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material
facePass: Eyes found in the colour map by remake/tools/bake/face.js (eyes.js) and written into the GLB as extras on the skinned mesh (face.eyes: per eye its centre, frame, outline and lid and lash colours, in bind space), for the eyelids the engine builds in code (engine/eyelids.js). The eyes are 0.42 m apart, 3.15 m up in the bind pose. Geometry and textures unchanged.
mouthPass: A jaw cut by remake/tools/bake/mouth.js: her lower beak is part of the one beak, so the pass parts it along the groove between the upper and the lower beak (the line given in the head frame, read off the beak's cross-sections where they are narrowest between the top and the bottom and smoothed, from behind the corner of the mouth to the tip at f = 1.26 m), in front of f = 0; snap=0.012 counts the vertices within 1.2 cm of the line as on it (the decimated groove runs along an edge loop: no triangle split, 555 vertices on the line, 320 opened, the lips 70 points from corner to corner), adds a Jaw bone under the Head at the hinge (1.21, 2.90, 0), blends the jaw in from the hinge to the cut, fills the mouth with a pocket (palate and tongue painted into a free corner of the colour map; 1,656 triangles) and writes face.mouth.talk = 6 (degrees the beak opens at the loudest syllable). channel=1 runs the pocket's fold along the middle of the long beak under the lips instead of back into the head, so the open beak shows no hole. No teeth. Re-exported with GLTFExporter (textures 1024 JPEG), node names and clip extras kept.
passes: decimateCommand, then bakeCommand, then faceCommand, then mouthCommand (the mouth pass takes its head frame from the eyes the face pass writes). Rebaking from the parts reproduces the GLB byte for byte.
lookCheck: qa/remake/shots/flugedla-look/ (the six views and the rig in the bind pose, the membrane weights of the long finger and of the body and thighs, the face, the beak open 6 and 15 degrees, the clips idle, walk, kink and happy), qa/remake/shots/flugedla-flight/ (takeOff, fly from the front and the three-quarter, glide, also from above and below, land, carry with a saddle stand-in on the seat), qa/remake/shots/flugedla-lineup/ (chapter=lineup: lineup, flugedla, flugedlaFace and the lineup without her), qa/remake/shots/flugedla-bench-r1/ and -r2/ (the GPU runs), qa/remake/shots/ptera-twin-now/ (the membrane in flight, plain and with back faces in magenta), qa/remake/shots/ptera-decimate/ (the parts after decimation) and qa/remake/shots/ptera-look/ (the source as received).
budget: GPU at the tablet preset, 1280x800 on the Iris Xe laptop, __benchmark medians, runs with and without her interleaved in one page load (six rounds each), two loads: she adds 0.15 to 0.82 ms, typically 0.3 to 0.55 (0.15 and 0.31 in the wide lineup, 0.39 to 0.82 in her own two shots). Whole frames: the wide lineup with all six characters 6.38 to 6.40 ms (6.08 to 6.24 without her), over 6 ms as it already was without her; her shots 4.65 to 7.13 ms (4.26 to 6.31 without her). Draw calls: she adds 2 (her skin and her quarter-level shadow caster): 50 in the wide lineup, 42 and 37 in her shots. Triangles: she adds 31,902 in the wide lineup (at 16 m her bind-pose diagonal of 9.7 m is about 470 px on screen, so her half level draws, 19,576, with the shadow caster's 12,326) and 51,480 in her shots (her 39,154 and the shadow caster), so the wide lineup is 317k triangles (285k without her) and her shots 305k and 358k, over 250k with the forest in view as they were without her. Textures: two 1024 px maps, 67.2 MB in all in the lineup.
notes: Coral-pink body, pale cream throat and belly, raspberry crest, peach wing membranes, long cream beak, big amber eyes, as in the concept; STYLE.md section 3 takes Flugeðla's row from this model. A pterosaur, not a dinosaur. Size: the owner chose the upper end of Pteranodon's range, a 7.5 m wingspan (5.6 to 7.6), so she can carry Egill; standing she is 4.2 m to the top of her crest. Friendly closed beak, no teeth. Known: folded on the ground, a membrane gathers into a soft bundle beside her, and inside the bundle many of its triangles turn over (from outside it reads as a fold, with a small notch at its edge near the hand); in flight, where the arm, the body and the thigh all pull on a membrane, its two faces come together or cross at under 1 % of the facing points, which the single-sided skin hides; opened wider than talking opens it (15 degrees), a sliver of the pocket shows at the beak's tip. A later chapter: she carries Egill on her back (carry, and the seat above).
